title: Workspace config (config.json)
description: The goal, the target organisations, the role families and their keywords, location classes, scoring weights, cadence and privacy settings for one workspace.

fictional.description: True only for the bundled demo workspace. Lets the demo live inside the engine repo.

timezone.description: IANA time zone name, for example Australia/Sydney. Sets what 'today' means.

writes_production_code.description: False means postings that expect production coding count as a lacking hard requirement until judged.

eligibility_cleared.description: Eligibility blocker types this person meets, so postings with them are not blocked.

targets.description: The organisations to target. Empty in a new workspace until the interview sets them; validate.py reports an empty list as an error and fetch_roles.py stops.

families.description: The role families to look for. Empty in a new workspace until the interview sets them; treated like empty targets.

top_n_for_gaps.description: How many top roles the gap leaderboard adds up over (per pool). Default 25.

gap_pool.description: overall (the default): one pool, the top roles overall. per_org: one pool per target organisation (its own top roles), so a gap at an organisation whose roles are not in the overall top still counts.

top_n_per_org_for_gaps.description: With gap_pool per_org: how many top roles per organisation. Default: top_n_for_gaps.

partially_verified_cap.description: Highest score a partially_verified item supports when its kind's self-reported cap is lower. Default 2. Never above 4, what corroborated evidence supports.

mode.description: weekly (the default): one full run a week, plus a run whenever something changes. The person decides.

build_up_weeks.description: Older configs: weeks of daily runs at the start. Default 0.

doors.description: Where scripts/fetch_doors.py looks for events: public Luma calendars, by their iCal feed address. Meetup, Eventbrite and LinkedIn are never fetched.

horizon_days.description: How far ahead to keep events. Default 120.

autopilot.description: Autopilot: a check-in that runs itself on the person's own schedule (skills/lvlme-autopilot). Every field is the person's answer, recorded by scripts/autopilot.py on their yes; LVLme never changes it on its own.

run.description: light: the top roles by fit plus new ones (scripts/run_plan.py); full: every role that needs judging.

sources.description: The read-only sources the person approved for runs with nobody present, in their words (for example github, website, gmail).

helpers.description: May unattended runs start helper agents (the judges and the blind reviewer)? Without them, new scores above 2 wait for review and count as 2.

scheduler.description: Where the schedule lives: a Claude desktop app scheduled task, or the computer's own scheduler running Claude Code.

sensitive_mode.description: Agent files (SUMMARY.md, dashboard.json) omit employer names, third-party names and salary.

share_contact_names_with_agents.description: Opt in to contact names in agent files. Ignored while sensitive_mode is true.

redact_terms.description: Employer names and other words to hide in sensitive mode.

extension.description: Extension field: any key starting x_ holds data the engine never reads (for example a field from an older system). Kept as is.

ats.description: The job board the organisation's careers page runs on. slug is its board name (Workable account, SmartRecruiters company); a Workday target names its careers page in careers_url instead.

region.description: Lever only: eu uses the EU endpoint.

ai_policy.description: The organisation's own published rules on candidates' use of AI, recorded only from its page (source). first_draft_by_person true: LVLme never writes this organisation's application answers, cover letters or résumé text; it writes a brief and reviews the person's own draft (method/CAMPAIGN.md).

source.description: The address of the organisation's page that states the policy.
